findings.message: The releasedAt fix is an instance fix. It adds `repoInstant`, which is a second copy of the reader's `isTime` + `new Date(at).toISOString()` (sync/specclaw.ts:108-111, `phaseTimesOf`). The two copies run on different hosts. `phaseTimesOf` runs in the reader (the plugin on the developer's machine, or wherever the self-sync runs), so a state.json `at` with no offset is read in that machine's time zone. `repoInstant` runs in `desired()` on the server for a push, so the same raw `phases.archived.at` is read in the server's time zone. A change's Released date and its `archived` phase time then disagree. The new test writes in the same host dependence: it expects `new Date("2026-10-17T03:12:41").toISOString()`, which passes on any host and so proves nothing. `Date.parse` also accepts V8's non-ISO legacy formats, which goes against B6. Fix: keep one normaliser, used by both the reader (phaseTimesOf, createdOf) and desired(). Make it explicit about a value with no offset (for example, read it as UTC the way createdOf reads a bare day, or treat it as unknown), and accept only ISO 8601 date and date-time forms. Pin the test to a fixed expected instant, not one computed from the host's time zone.
findings.scenario: The plugin runs on a laptop in Asia/Colombo (UTC+05:30) and the server runs in UTC. state.json has archived {status:"done", at:"2026-10-17T03:12:41"}. The push stores phaseTimes.archived = 2026-10-16T21:42:41Z but released_at = 2026-10-17T03:12:41Z: one proposal, two different archive instants 5.5 h apart. Separately, releasedAt "1" or "Oct 17" parses and is stored as 2001-01-01 or 2001-10-17 instead of null.

findings.message: The 'one read rule' gives two answers. `isRead` needs a non-empty ref before `@<sha>` (`search > 0`), but `refOf` (withdraw.ts) and the author walk use the bare `AT_SHA`, which also matches a source with no ref. The new rule also stops rejecting whitespace, which the old READ did, so arbitrary text ending in `@<sha>` now counts as a read. Fix: put the ref requirement into the shared regex (for example `^(?=\S)(\S+)@(SHA)$`) so every caller applies the same rule.
findings.scenario: Source "@4f2c9a1": isRead gives false, so the phase read is dropped, but refOf gives "", so withdrawal sees the ref "" and the author walk takes the sha 4f2c9a1. Source "the repo@4f2c9a1": isRead now gives true, although the AC-3 test treats "the repo" as made-up text.
